Thousands of migrants surge into Spain's Ceuta enclave, dozens dead

Thousands of migrants, primarily from sub-Saharan Africa, surged into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco. At least 72 deaths were reported amidst the influx. Spain deployed military forces and decided to erect a new border barrier to manage the situation. Thousands of migrants have since begun returning to Morocco. The event has led to an international crisis, with Spanish leaders criticizing European partners over immigration policies.
